newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National says to get ScotAm detail soon.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National says to get ScotAm detail soon.

text.p: Britain's Abbey National Plc said on Monday it hoped it would soon get more information from Scottish Amicable so it could reassess its bid for the mutually-owned life assurance group.

"We anticipated getting more information this week, at which stage we will be signing a confidentiality agreement. After that we will not be able to say anything," Abbey National spokesman Chris Wermann told Reuters.

Wermann said Abbey, which two weeks ago launched a surprise bid for ScotAm valuing it at up to 1.4 billion pounds ($2.30 billion), had not changed its initial offer, adding newspaper reports of a 2.2 billion pound bid were "purely speculative".

Abbey's offer for ScotAm, which last month announced two stage plans to drop its mutual status and float on the London stock exchange, opened the floodgates to speculation that other financial services groups would bid for the group.

Britain's Prudential Corp entered the fray last week with a 1.9 billion pound bid, but other firms rumoured to be in the running have not made any public overtures. Australian Mutal Provident Society (AMP) has said it is keen to make acquisitions in Britain and one newspaper report said it had already asked ScotAm for access to financial information on the group.

Abbey's Wermann said the rules governing mutual groups in Britain meant ScotAm would not have to reveal offers made to it until it decided if it had a preferred bid. This meant that other firms could make offers for the group without them becoming public. "It will be be behind closed doors negotiations from now on," he added.
